name: Dog Supplies Checklist
description: A category-by-category dog supplies shopping list for new puppy and adult dog owners.

items.note: Match puppy, adult or senior formula and keep the dog's current food during the transition

items.text: Stainless steel or ceramic food bowl
Water bowl, refilled with fresh water daily
Correctly sized crate, with a divider for puppies
Quiet, draft-free spot to place the crate
ID tag with your name and phone number
Chew toys suited to the dog's size and chewing strength
Fetch toys such as balls or tug ropes
Brush or comb suited to the coat type
Designated outdoor potty area or routine

faq.q: What supplies do I need before bringing a dog home?
faq.a: Have food, food and water bowls, a crate or bed, a collar with ID, a leash, a few toys, basic grooming tools and cleanup supplies ready before the dog arrives.

faq.q: What size crate should I buy for my dog?
faq.a: Choose a crate large enough for the dog to stand, turn around and lie down comfortably. For puppies, buy an adult-size crate with a divider so you can expand the space as they grow.

faq.q: Do I need different supplies for a puppy versus an adult dog?
faq.a: The categories are the same, but puppies need life-stage food, smaller or adjustable gear and extra training supplies like pads and chews. Replace outgrown items as the puppy develops.

faq.q: Should I consult a vet about food and parasite prevention?
faq.a: Yes. This list is general guidance. Confirm diet, vaccinations and flea, tick and worm prevention with a veterinarian for your specific dog.

faq.q: Can I print this dog supplies checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can carry it to the pet store and check off each category as you go.
